transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-02-09
Start: 15:30 UTC
Duration: 44 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Ravi Patel (Sable Tech Head of Search), Lina Gomez (ML Engineer), Markus He (Platform Lead)
---
Auto-summary: show hosted embeddings endpoint, demo rerank API, Console walkthrough (Optimize recommendations), discuss security/VPC and pilot next steps

00:00:03 Maya: alright good afternoon everyone, um thanks for joining, i think we've got about 45 minutes, i'll be quick on intros — i'm Maya, AE at Redwood, with Diego our solutions engineer.
00:00:12 Ravi: hey thanks, ravi here, we'll jump in, we've been evaluating vector stores and thinking about reranking to improve our ecom search relevance
00:00:18 Diego: awesome. quick agenda, we'll demo the hosted embeddings endpoint, then the reranker flow (candidate retrieval -> embeddings -> rerank), show the Console for observability and Optimize suggestions, then Q&A and next steps. sound good?
00:00:30 Lina: yup, sounds great. we care most about latency for product page search and cost per query.
00:00:36 Markus: and security, we need encryption at rest with KMS, SSO and audit logs.

00:03:05 Diego: jumping into the API — first the embeddings call. i'll paste a curl: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/embeddings -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" -d '{"input":"red wool sweater, size m","model":"rwd-embed-compact-512"}'. the response gives a 512-d float vector, normalized by default.
00:03:35 Lina: small question — do you always normalize? we use cosine sims primarily
00:03:40 Diego: yes we normalize on the client side in our SDK if you want, but the hosted embeddings are L2-normalized by default so cosine is equivalent to dot for ranking. that helps with consistent scoring across dims.
00:04:02 Ravi: what about dimensionality options? 512 vs 768 tradeoffs?
00:04:08 Diego: good callout. 512 reduces storage and per-query compute; 768 sometimes gives slightly better recall. Optimize can recommend model/quantization based on your recall SLO from sample evals.
00:05:10 Maya: switching to rerank. our typical flow we recommend: Retriever (approx nearest neighbor, e.g., Pinecone or your own ANN) to fetch top 100, then we do a small cross-encoder rerank using the Redwood rerank endpoint which calls a lightweight cross-attention model — it's a hosted API you call with the candidate texts and query.
00:05:30 Lina: do you have a demo sample?
00:05:32 Diego: yep i'll show an end-to-end. i'll simulate retrieval by returning 12 candidates from our sample index, then post to /v1/rerank with payload: {"query":"best wool sweater for winter","candidates":[...],"model":"rwd-ranker-small"}. Response is ranked_ids + scores.
00:06:00 (screen share noise)
00:06:04 Markus: small nit — how expensive is that per candidate? we can't rerank thousands per q; we typically rerank top 10-50.
00:06:13 Diego: exactly, we recommend reranking top K where K is typically 10-50. cost scales linearly with candidates for cross-encoder style models. Optimize can recommend split approach: a cheap fast-scorer to get to 100 then a higher-quality cross-encoder for top 10.
00:07:00 Ravi: and latency? our SLO is 150ms p95 on product search queries.
00:07:06 Diego: hosted can deliver ~70-150ms p95 depending on model size and sequence length. for tighter SLOs we propose Dedicated reserved capacity or edge routing. we showed in benchmarks that rwd-ranker-small on hosted at 512 tokens median was ~45ms for the rerank call alone, but end-to-end retrieval + rerank pushes p95; caching prefixes and KV cache reduces repeated prompt cost.
00:08:00 Lina: you mentioned caching — how does that plug in?
00:08:05 Diego: Redwood runtime has prefix/KV caching; for rerank we cache encoded candidate KV entries so repeated candidates don't re-encode. Console Optimize will show cache hit rates and suggests TTLs.
00:08:30 Maya: jumping to Console — Diego, can you show the route-level latency breakdown?
00:08:36 Diego: sure. (console nav) here you see per-route token counts, p50/p95 latency, and cost per 1k tokens. under Optimize tab we surface batching suggestions and quantization toggles. for example, it suggests dynamic batching for low qps with a 20ms batching window to save ~18%/token.
00:09:20 Ravi: interesting, we saw similar gains with batching in our experiments. but concern: batching increases tail latency sometimes.
00:09:27 Diego: yep tradeoff — Optimize gives simulations: if you set batch window to 20ms expected latency goes up 10ms but tokens per second improves and cost drops. you can set per-route SLOs and the platform enforces fallback to single-request mode when tail approaches SLO.
00:10:10 Markus: security questions: VPC/private deployment — we need to know whether hosted keeps logs, and how KMS integration works.
00:10:18 Maya: good Q. hosted stores minimal audit logs for debugging; by default payloads are processed in-host but you can opt into Private deployment or Dedicated with VPC peering for strict isolation. we support customer-managed KMS for encryption at rest and bring-your-own-key for Private. we'll share SOC2 and ISO artifacts.
00:10:45 Markus: what about retention windows for logs?
00:10:48 Maya: default 30 days for logs with configurable retention for enterprise. retention and access are controlled via RBAC and SSO/SAML.
00:11:20 Lina: curious about integration effort — we run on k8s and use OpenSearch for candidate retrieval. does Redwood require a specific vector store?
00:11:27 Diego: no — Redwood's hosted embeddings and reranker are agnostic. you can use any ANN store (Pinecone, Milvus, OpenSearch) or your own. we provide SDK helpers and a reference pipeline (retriever -> rerank) in our examples repo.
00:12:00 Ravi: can reranker operate with a single API call that returns final ranked docs (i.e., retrieval + rerank in one)?
00:12:08 Diego: not currently as a single managed call when using external ANN stores; we keep retrieval decoupled so customers can use their store. for customers who want a fully managed pipeline we offer Redwood Dedicated + integrated vector store in roadmap (we mentioned that last quarter).
00:13:10 Maya: quick note on cost: embeddings are charged per 1k input tokens/vectors; rerank calls charged per candidate-token ops. We'll include estimated cost for your traffic in the pilot proposal.
00:14:00 (demo sample searches)
00:15:05 Diego: showing a failure mode — when candidate set has near-duplicates, cross-encoder helps push the more relevant doc up. see here example: query "waterproof hiking boot" top retrieval returns 3 that are generic; rerank surfaces product with "Gore-Tex" mention higher.
00:16:22 Lina: do you support custom reranker fine-tuning or soft prompts?
00:16:27 Diego: at the moment we support instruction tuning via prompt templates and scoring weight adjustments. fine-tuning of cross-encoders is an enterprise add-on — we can discuss offline.
00:17:05 Ravi: ok good. for our holiday catalog we had a big spike — how does Redwood handle bursty traffic?
00:17:12 Maya: Dedicated has reserved pools and burst capacity; hosted has autoscaling but bursts can increase cost. Optimize will estimate burst cost and recommend reserved capacity breakpoints.
00:18:00 Markus: we need SLOs and SLA language — can you provide that?
00:18:05 Maya: yes we'll include SLA matrix in the pilot addendum (99.9% uptime on Dedicated, hosted varies by tier).
00:20:00 (brief digression on embedding quantization)
00:20:10 Diego: quantization options: 8-bit/4-bit post-training quantization for embeddings storage reduces footprint ~2-4x with minor recall impact; Optimize suggests quantization levels from sample eval metrics.
00:21:15 Lina: show us an example of Optimize suggestion?
00:21:20 Diego: (Console) here's an Optimize suggestion: for route /search, it recommends: "Enable dynamic batching window 20ms; enable prefix KV cache for product descriptions; use rwd-embed-compact-512 and 8-bit quantization" with expected 22% cost savings and <2% recall drop on sample set.
00:22:00 Ravi: that sounds promising. we'd want to run our own eval suite — can we upload sample prompts/labels?
00:22:07 Diego: yes, Console supports uploading eval sets. we can run regression checks per rollout and fire alerts when MRR drops.
00:23:50 Markus: any compliance folks on your side?
00:23:55 Maya: security & compliance will participate in the next call; we'll include the security pack and a contact for SOC2 queries.
00:24:30 Lina: what's the timeline to get a pilot running? we want ~2 weeks to validate quality and perf.
00:24:36 Maya: realistic — 1-2 weeks to stand up a hosted pilot (token keys + sample data + small traffic), 2-3 weeks for detailed perf results.
00:25:10 Diego: i'll outline the micro-benchmark we'll run: 10k docs, simulate 100 qps bursts and 5 qps steady, measure p50/p95 end-to-end for hosted and a dedicated config.
00:26:00 (customer clarifying dataset)
00:27:10 Ravi: our dataset has many near-duplicates and long product descriptions (avg 250 tokens), will that change latency?
00:27:18 Diego: yes sequence length impacts token processing — reranker tokenization and cross-attention scale with sequence length. Optimize will recommend truncation strategy and candidate snippet extraction to keep effective token count reasonable.
00:28:30 Lina: about metrics — we'll want MRR, NDCG and p95 latency tracked.
00:28:36 Diego: absolutely Console exposes custom metrics dashboards for that.
00:30:00 (15-minute live benchmark teaser)
00:35:00 Maya: ok wrapping up, let's recap next steps and owners.
00:35:10 Maya: Diego, you'll run the perf micro-benchmark and share numbers; Maya will send pilot proposal and security docs; Markus will send compliance checklist.
00:35:30 Markus: agreed. also please include a sample contract with data residency options.
00:36:00 Ravi: thanks — we'll review and aim to have internal sign-off by end of Feb.
00:36:12 Lina: any follow up call cadence?
00:36:16 Maya: propose a 30-min POC kick-off the week of 2027-02-22 and weekly 30-min check-ins during the pilot.
00:37:05 Diego: quick note — link to sample demo notebook: https://github.com/redwood-inference/examples/tree/main/embeddings-rerank and security pack: https://redwood.ai/security-pack.pdf
00:38:10 (brief chitchat)
00:42:00 Maya: thanks everyone, we'll send notes and action items.
00:42:20 Ravi: great, thanks Maya, Diego.
00:42:28 Meeting end.

Post-call recap block:
- Pilot scope: Hosted embeddings + rerank for product search on a 10k sample dataset. 2-week pilot with perf benchmarks comparing hosted vs dedicated.
- Links shared: demo notebook, security pack, pricing sheet (to be sent).
- Next scheduled: pilot contract & perf test by 2027-02-16; POC kickoff week of 2027-02-22.
